title: Machine Learning for Computational Sensing Research Intern
description: Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally? ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. The Analog Garage is ADI’s research & innovation lab, located in the heart of downtown Boston. We pioneer breakthrough technologies to solve high-impact problems that drive tangible value. Bringing together engineers, research scientists, and business leaders, we develop new technologies and solutions in a fast-paced and evidence-driven innovation culture. About the role The Algorithmic Solutions Group at the Garage develops cutting-edge, efficient algorithms to bring intelligence to the physical world. We fuse state-of-the-art machine learning with deep domain expertise to convert raw physical data into actionable insights, solving the hard problems where off-the-shelf solutions fall short. We are looking for a motivated research intern to develop algorithms for a high-impact biomedical sensing project, applying novel AI and signal processing techniques to interpret noisy, real-world radio-frequency (RF) signals from highly lossy media. You will collaborate closely with researchers across RF systems, machine learning, and signal processing, while being bounded by practical signal chain constraints. What you'll do Design and prototype algorithms to advance the state of the art in computational RF sensing, spanning analytical and learning-based methods for clutter suppression, detection, and reconstruction, as well as hardware-algorithm co-design. Use software simulations and real-world data to demonstrate feasibility and evaluate algorithm performance. Document results as internal technical reports, with opportunities to publish in top-tier conferences or journals based on the significance of findings. Required qualifications Enrolled in a PhD program with a concentration in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Preference will be given to candidates within two years of completing their PhD. Strong fundamentals in machine learning, deep learning, and signal processing. Proficiency in Python and ML frameworks (PyTorch or TensorFlow). Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills. Preferred qualifications You’ll stand out with one or more of the qualifications below. Even if you don’t meet these points or aren’t sure, we encourage you to apply. Tell us about your research, interests, and the perspective you would bring to the team. Strong publication record in top conferences or journals. Interest in biomedical sensing. Experience in AI/ML for computational sensing or imaging, and inverse problems. Familiarity with RF signals and systems for sensing or imaging is a plus. Experience in AI/ML and optimization for hardware-algorithm co-design. Domain knowledge in wave physics or electromagnetic simulation and modeling. Candidates should have experience in one or more of the following areas: signal processing; machine learning and artificial intelligence; graph, network and distributed algorithms; circuit modeling and numerical simulation; power networks and power system engineering; software engineering; optimization; and statistical modeling and simulation. Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate, and advance faster than ever.
